3.old: Chilliwack Proper West is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it. The closest official description is the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan area, which covers the established residential area of Chilliwack Proper as a whole.
3.new: Chilliwack Proper West is used by the MLS® as a sub-area name within the City of Chilliwack, and the City has no published boundary for it. The nearest official description is the neighbourhood plan called Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan, whose area takes in the established residential part of Chilliwack Proper taken as a whole.

38.old: Chilliwack is in School District 33 (SD33). SD33’s Long Range Facilities Plan says its elementary schools are kindergarten to grade 5, its middle schools grades 6 to 8 and its secondary schools grades 9 to 12.
38.new: The schools in Chilliwack are part of School District 33 (SD33). According to SD33’s Long Range Facilities Plan, elementary schools run from kindergarten to grade 5, middle schools cover grades 6 to 8, and secondary schools cover grades 9 to 12.

95.old: Quoted in a City of Chilliwack public hearing notice dated May 4, 2021, for a rezoning inside the plan area
95.new: Quoted from a May 4, 2021 notice of public hearing by the City of Chilliwack, which concerned a rezoning in the plan area.

101.old: Lot size (FVREB MLS® recorded sales data): the median lot size of detached houses sold in recent 2026 MLS® activity was 6,136 sq ft, based on 14 sales with a recorded lot size.
101.new: FVREB MLS® recorded sales data shows a median lot size of 6,136 sq ft for the detached houses that sold in recent 2026 MLS® activity. The figure comes from 14 sales that had a recorded lot size.

122.old: Flood: under the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519, habitable floor space in areas protected by a standard dike must be at or above the applicable Flood Construction Level, plus 0.6 m of freeboard.
122.new: Flood: Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519, the City’s bylaw, requires habitable floor space in areas with standard dike protection to sit no lower than the applicable Flood Construction Level, with 0.6 m of freeboard added.

123.old: The City has an ongoing $30 million program to raise the dyke system to the current provincial elevation, and the Young Road dyke has been upgraded.
123.new: The City is running a $30 million program, still under way, to bring the dyke system up to the provincial elevation as it stands now, and the Young Road dyke has already received its upgrade.

129.old: Ask the City what the Residential 1 and Residential 2 designations allow on the lots around the home, since the plan is about infill.
129.new: Because the plan is about infill, the City can say what Residential 1 and Residential 2 designations let you do on lots near the home.

150.old: Chilliwack Proper West is an MLS® sub-area name. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it. The closest official description is the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan area.
150.new: As an MLS® sub-area name, Chilliwack Proper West has no boundary published by the City. The closest official description is that of the City’s Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan.

152.old: That is an orientation from addresses, not a City boundary, so ask me if a specific address is in it.
152.new: This describes the area by addresses and is not an official City boundary, so ask me whether a particular address falls inside it.

155.old: Route 59 Industrial runs between Downtown Chilliwack and Cottonwood Mall via the Lickman Park and Ride. BC Transit’s page shows peak-period weekday trips only
155.new: BC Transit’s Route 59 Industrial links Downtown Chilliwack with Cottonwood Mall by way of the Lickman Park and Ride, and its page lists weekday trips in the peak periods only.

157.old: Route 66 Fraser Valley Express is a regional route between Chilliwack and Lougheed Town Centre Station, via Carvolth Exchange, Highstreet Exchange and McCallum Park and Ride. Its Chilliwack stops are Downtown Chilliwack, Vedder Rd at Luckakuck Way and the Lickman Park and Ride
157.new: The regional Route 66 Fraser Valley Express connects Chilliwack with Lougheed Town Centre Station, going by way of McCallum Park and Ride, Highstreet Exchange and Carvolth Exchange. In Chilliwack it stops at the Lickman Park and Ride, Vedder Rd at Luckakuck Way and Downtown Chilliwack.

172.old: Under the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519, habitable floor space in areas protected by a standard dike must be at or above the applicable Flood Construction Level, plus 0.6 m of freeboard.
172.new: The City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519 sets a rule for areas protected by a standard dike: habitable floor space has to be set at or over the Flood Construction Level that applies, with 0.6 m of freeboard on top.

173.old: The City has an ongoing $30 million program to raise the dyke system, and the Young Road dyke has been upgraded.
173.new: Chilliwack’s dyke system is being raised under an ongoing $30 million City program, and the dyke at Young Road is now upgraded.
